Observation Details: Edit after the fact (2/14/2018): this observation on 2/2/2018 was the first time I saw Kites in this tree. I have seen them several times since - they always seem to arrive just before sunset. So far, six is still the high count, but they have been there every day I have looked for them at sunset (which is now several times). They are near the top of a tall deciduous tree behind the backyards on the west side of Acton (around this 2128 address).

As with many other days, when I looked for them (from Charlie Dorr park) at about 30 minutes before sunset, they weren't there. But when I walked past right at sunset (~5:50), there were three. Most I have seen in this tree is six at a time (that was slightly later - maybe more would have come this time had I waited).

Three seen in the roosting (?) tree that I have reported previously (https://ebird.org/view/checklist/S42445216) that is roughly behind 2128 Acton (west of the street, behind the houses). Today there were three but I have seen up to six. The tree can be seen from Charlie Doerr Park from the back gate or from the sidewalk in front of the front gate (from the play structure, the tree in question is blocked by a redwood).Maybe these are the birds that are often seen during the day at Cesar Chavez & Albany Bulb & Meeker Slough? Started the checklist at sunrise on the summit of Eagle Peak, and birded from the summit down, through Deer Flat, and out Mitchell Canyon to visitor's centre. In retrospect, I should have split it into multiple checklists. Will do so next time. General thoughts on locations: Lazuli buntings all at the top near Eagle Peak. Black-throated Grey and Hermit Warblers also mostly up high. Cassin's Vireo and all the Woodpeckers were in the oak woodland around Deer Flat. Townsend's Warblers were everywhere, and to a lesser degree Yellow-Rumped Warblers too. Nashville and Wilson's Warblers I did not see up high - only from Deer Flat on down.

Hiking with my daughter (6mo). All species I could ID are reported, but I wasn't birding as thoroughly as I might have otherwise. Hiked from Mitchell Canyon, over Eagle Peak, and looped back via Meridian Ridge and Back Creek

I also saw an oriole, that I am 90% sure was a Bullock's, but there is a small chance it was a Hooded, so I am leaving it off the checklist.

Observation Details: Reporting this (would have used “Galliformes sp.” were it available) because I am relatively sure I saw a Vanuatu Scrubfowl, but they seem rare enough and it was a poor-enough look that I want to be cautious. It was a black, Galliform-type bird, about 30cm head to tail, that flushed from one side of road (from area of long grass which I realize isn’t ideal habitat) and flew low across the road and into bush on other side.   Bulky body, small head, small wings. I could only see black but it was a brief look with bare eyes from ~5-10m so I could have missed markings. On Elluk Plateau. I can’t think what else it could be except for a small, black, feral domestic chicken - but then the flight (awkward, but flew for at least 10-15 meters that I could see) seemed too capable for a feral chicken. I note there is ID’ed scrubfowl habitat not too far away on Pango peninsula, but this is a few km from there.
